clue.text: Opening meant for training someone to do the dirty work

definitions.text: someone to do the dirty work

parts.note: a hatch is an opening in a deck, wall or floor

indicators.note: training puts recruits through drills that reshape them, so the word before it is put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is reading an opening that was intended to train a recruit for unpleasant jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchet man is a person employed to carry out unpleasant tasks such as sackings or smears on someone else's behalf.

clue.text: Upset Eliot with wrong covers

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting something tips it over so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the poet T. S. Eliot, by his initials
and means together with
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: An offended Eliot finds his errors being concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliot is not used whole: the poet is reduced to his initials, which are then flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand in is to deputise, the same as covering for an absent colleague, so the phrase and the verb are synonyms.

clue.text: Revolting Ruth is being arrogant

parts.note: people in revolt are up in arms, or simply up
ruth is an old word for compassion, surviving in ruthless

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth behaves in a disgusting, haughty way.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth looks like a name, but here it is the archaic noun meaning pity, the opposite of ruthlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity is an informal adjective for someone self-important who acts above their station, close to arrogant.

clue.text: Old guides upset over shows

indicators.note: turned over, a run of letters is read the other way round, upwards in this down entry
the words show the answer within them, displaying it in plain sight

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second run together

explanation.surface: Former tour guides, upset, put on performances.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset is part of the hiding place, not an anagram signal; the reversal signal is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Used describes something second-hand, previously owned, which is one sense of old.

clue.text: Writer's offspring a rich family member

parts.note: the American novelist Philip Roth, with the possessive
a child is offspring

explanation.surface: An author's son or daughter belongs to a wealthy dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rothschilds are the famous European banking dynasty, so any one of them is a member of a wealthy family.

clue.text: Revolutionary entertainment for VIP

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fairground ride that turns round and round
second meaning: an important, influential person

explanation.surface: Some radical form of amusement is laid on for an important guest.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary hints at politics, but it means rotating: the fairground Ferris wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a Ferris wheel at a fair and, informally, a person with power or influence.

clue.text: Country widely recognised as stunner and very, very old

parts.note: a knockout, a blow that stuns
so means very, as in so good
V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A country celebrated as a beauty that is ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated very is used twice over, once as a word and once as an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008 and is recognised as a sovereign state by many, though not all, governments.

clue.text: With Rex, close to George Galloway's home?

parts.note: by can mean with, as in by hand
R is short for Rex, king

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: A question about where the Scottish politician George Galloway lives, perhaps alongside a king.
explanation.walkthrough: George Galloway is a well-known British politician, but Galloway here is a Scottish breed of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a cowshed, so it is where a Galloway cow is kept; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Advice concerning article earlier — it might be taken on board

definitions.text: it might be taken on board

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tip is a piece of advice
as to means concerning
placement only: says the article comes before the rest

explanation.surface: A recommendation about something earlier that someone might take on board, like a suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: Earlier tells you the article goes in front. Taken on board suggests heeding advice, but the board is a dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is an Italian starter, food that might be eaten at the table, board being an old word for a table spread with food.

clue.text: Press and why it doesn't usually mean what it says

definitions.text: it doesn't usually mean what it says

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
the letter Y is pronounced like the word why

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about why the press rarely means what it prints.
explanation.walkthrough: Press looks like the newspapers, but it is the household chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is saying the opposite of what is meant, so an ironic statement does not mean its literal sense.

clue.text: Frank swallows tablet coated with sugar

indicators.note: something that swallows takes another thing inside itself

parts.note: frank and candid both mean open and honest
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A man called Frank takes a sugar-coated pill.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a name, but it is the adjective; E for an ecstasy pill is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied fruit or peel has been preserved by cooking in sugar syrup, leaving it sugar-coated.

clue.text: Why no facilities in the house?

indicators.note: being in a place means sitting inside it, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: a house is a home
O is a nought, zero, nothing
facilities is a euphemism for toilet, a WC

explanation.surface: A puzzled question: why is there no toilet in the house?
explanation.definitionFit: How come is an informal way of asking why something is so.

clue.text: Old paramilitaries mentioned in paper

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken out, so the letters are judged by their sound when said

parts.note: the SA, the Nazi Brownshirts, said as two letter names

explanation.surface: A newspaper mentions a defunct paramilitary group.
explanation.walkthrough: The SA were the Nazi stormtroopers; saying S and A out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper is a written academic piece, a sense shared with an essay set as coursework.

clue.text: Rebuked conspiracy theorist interrupting gent

indicators.note: one who interrupts breaks into the middle of something, so goes inside it

parts.note: a toff is a posh gentleman
David Icke, the British conspiracy theorist, written surname then initial

explanation.surface: A conspiracy theorist butting in on a gentleman got told off.
explanation.walkthrough: David Icke is a notorious British conspiracy theorist; his name goes in as ICKE D. A toff is British slang for an upper-class man.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticked off is an informal phrase for scolded or reprimanded, a synonym of rebuked.

clue.text: Dorset team cursed flukes

indicators.note: a cursed thing is blighted or messed up, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Dorset sports side swore at their lucky breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Flukes look like lucky chances, but they are parasitic flatworms.
explanation.definitionFit: Trematodes are a class of parasitic flatworms commonly called flukes, such as the liver fluke.

clue.text: Shelf causing superficial injury?

parts.note: surface reading: a sharp shelf edge grazes someone
setter's reading: the answer describes its own wordplay, as a word for meat whose letters, once wound or twisted, become shelf

explanation.surface: Someone has caught themselves on a shelf and suffered a minor cut.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer's first word twisted gives shelf, and wound, said to rhyme with sound, signals the twisting.
explanation.definitionFit: A flesh wound is an injury that breaks the skin without damaging bones or organs, a superficial hurt.

clue.text: 'Ridiculous!' claimed Tories about current rules of behaviour

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled words go round the next part
something ridiculous is absurd and nonsensical, so the following words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
in means current, fashionable

explanation.surface: Conservatives dismissed criticism of the present ethical standards as ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters are split after their first letter to wrap round IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ministerial Code is the UK government's rulebook setting out the standards of conduct expected of ministers.

clue.text: Pay hospital in betrayal of principles

indicators.note: in places one part inside another, here within the phrase that follows

parts.note: a sellout is an abandonment of one's principles for gain
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Hospital pay arrangements are criticised as a betrayal of principles.
explanation.definitionFit: To shell out is an informal phrasal verb meaning to pay money, often reluctantly.

clue.text: Rash's gone away on bust

parts.note: someone out has gone away
to bust something is to break it; on simply places this piece after

explanation.surface: A skin rash has disappeared from someone's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: Rash's reads as rash is, and bust looks like the chest but is the verb to break.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash can mean a sudden spate of something, such as a rash of burglaries, which is an outbreak.

clue.text: Arthur's first minder worked with us — a female one

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or shaped, so the letters are worked into a new order
first asks for only the opening letter of the name

parts.note: the initial of the name
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A minder who looked after young Arthur worked alongside us, and she was a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on minder: a female one of those. Minder serves both as anagram letters and as the noun the definition refers back to.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after children, a female child-minder.

clue.text: Clear vacant land up and finally solve mystery

parts.note: to rid is to clear

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters run from bottom to top
vacant means emptied, so the inside of the word is cleared out leaving its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters, then flipped

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Instructions to clear empty ground and finally crack a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzling question or something baffling, a mystery to be worked out.

clue.text: Chuck and Di's time with children

parts.note: Di, the short name used for Princess Diana
T is the abbreviation for time
CH is a dictionary abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: Charles and Diana's time with their children, Chuck being a nickname for Prince Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: Chuck and Di suggests the royal couple Charles and Diana, but chuck is the verb to throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to get rid of or abandon it, the same as chucking it.

clue.text: Sad lady leaving city gets bottom pinched

indicators.note: pinched means gripped between two parts, so one piece is held inside the other
something leaving departs, so those letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
LA is Los Angeles
the rear is the bottom, backside

explanation.surface: An unhappy woman leaves town after being groped.
explanation.walkthrough: The city removed from lady leaves DY, which then holds the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means gloomy and depressing, a sense close to sad.

clue.text: Gentleman went undercover since stealing fifty

parts.note: to go under cover is to hide

indicators.note: something stealing takes a thing and holds it, so one part is taken inside another

parts.note: ago and since both refer back in time, as in long ago
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A gentleman thief has been in hiding since taking fifty pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of the Spanish lower nobility, a gentleman by birth.

clue.text: Want quiet in garden

indicators.note: in places one part inside another, here within the gardening word

parts.note: to hoe is to work the garden
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Longing for some peace in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To hope for something is to wish for it, a synonym of want as a verb.

clue.text: I'm going for toast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a casual British goodbye
second meaning: a word said when raising glasses

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are going to make some toast.
explanation.walkthrough: Toast looks like breakfast, but it is a drinking salute; cheerio is a British informal goodbye and was once used as a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is said when leaving, meaning goodbye, and was formerly a toast like cheers.

clue.text: Pretty smart

definitions.meaning: first meaning: attractive in an endearing way

explanation.walkthrough: Pretty smart reads as fairly clever, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means charmingly attractive and, especially in American use, also clever or shrewd.

clue.text: Dish with sauce sent back for seconds with Ramsay cursing

indicators.note: a dish sent back is returned, so the letters go the other way

parts.note: sauce and lip both mean cheek, impudence

indicators.note: seconds asks for the second letter of each of the following words

parts.note: second letter
second letter

explanation.surface: A meal is returned to the kitchen for more as Gordon Ramsay swears.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauce and seconds look like food, but sauce is cheek and seconds means second letters. Gordon Ramsay is a famously foul-mouthed TV chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is a dish of rice cooked in stock with spices, often with meat or vegetables.

clue.text: Join teaching assistant in brook

parts.note: to enter a club or contest is to join it
TA is the usual abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone joins a classroom helper in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Brook looks like a stream, but it is the verb meaning to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook an idea is to tolerate or allow it, and to entertain an idea means to consider or admit it.
